title: E6 task-decoding checkpoint form B
instructions: Read this original practice prompt and make all three task-decoding decisions before submitting. Prompt: The Neighbourhood Youth Website invites articles for local teenage readers. Write about one idea learned in a school subject that you have used, or could use, to improve how people share a community space. Explain one specific actual or realistic situation and what the idea might achieve.

parts.prompt: What is the main command, or thinking job, in this prompt?

options.text: Describe every community space in the neighbourhood.
Explain how one school-learned idea can improve the sharing of a community space in one specific situation.
Argue that teenagers should control all public spaces.
Compare the difficulty of all school subjects.

choice_rationales.A: The prompt narrows the response to one idea and one application rather than a survey of spaces.
choice_rationales.B: This captures the explanatory transfer, the target setting and the specific-situation requirement.
choice_rationales.C: No claim about control or authority is requested.
choice_rationales.D: The school subject supplies an idea; subjects themselves are not being compared.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The writer must explain how one school-learned idea could improve one specific use of shared space.

options.text: Local teenage readers of the Neighbourhood Youth Website

choice_rationales.A: The writing situation names both the local context and teenage readers.
choice_rationales.B: A teacher may assess the response but is not its imagined reader.
choice_rationales.C: The prompt does not require specialist professional knowledge.
choice_rationales.D: The website is addressed to teenagers, not younger children.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The article should use clear, relevant language for local teenage readers.

parts.prompt: Which proposed focus best satisfies the scope and personal-application requirements?

options.text: Use the scientific idea of observing before changing variables to test a booking board for a crowded community court, then explain what fairer scheduling might achieve.
List every scientific idea learned since primary school.
Describe why community spaces are important without applying a school-learned idea.
Invent several unrelated improvements for parks, libraries and roads without one specific situation.

choice_rationales.A: This selects one school idea, one shared space, one realistic use and an intended result.
choice_rationales.B: A list breaks the one-idea limit and lacks application.
choice_rationales.C: The broad theme omits the required transfer from school learning.
choice_rationales.D: Several settings and unrelated changes break the specific-situation scope.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The booking-board focus creates one bounded, realistic application and explains what the school-learned method could achieve.
